incumbent.name: Doug Vantlin
incumbent.party: Republican (party not confirmed in a source fetched for this profile)
incumbent.summary: Vantlin took office in 2019, according to candidate John Fuller {wtwo_five}, and is reaching the end of his permitted time in office, so he is not on the ballot {wtwo_five}. His tenure included completion of a $36 million jail expansion {vsc_jail}.
record: 2019: Began his first term; candidate John Fuller said he was promoted to major when Vantlin took office {wtwo_five}.

February 2024: The $36 million Knox County Jail expansion, funded by a bond sale, a jail tax and remaining American Rescue Plan Act money, was nearing completion; it added holding cells, more padded rooms and a dedicated medical unit. Vantlin said, "We're crowded in the old part, and this is going to give us more room to work" {vsc_jail}.

October 2025: After the county council set two promoted officers' salaries at deputy rather than sergeant level while adopting the 2026 budget, Vantlin said the sheriff's merit board had approved the promotions in August 2025 and that the council's role is limited to funding positions; Council President Mike Morris said the council had not known of the merit board approval and could adjust pay by later ordinance {vsc_correction}.

August 2026: Vantlin said state law requires sheriffs to honor ICE detainer requests and that the jail holds detainees up to 48 hours; he said five detainees had been held in the county since Jan. 1 (two transferred to ICE, one released, two held on local charges) {vsc_ice}.
Candidate John Fuller, the office's chief deputy, put the office's annual budget at more than $8 million {vsc_forum}.

race_context: Open seat: Sheriff Doug Vantlin is reaching the end of his permitted time in office {wtwo_five}.
Five candidates filed: Republicans John Fuller, Michael Fisher, Paul Jones and Dan Short, and Democrat Brian Hagen {vsc_forum}.

May 5, 2026 Republican primary (unofficial): Dan Short 2,155 votes (40.55%), Michael Fisher 27.98%, John Fuller 18.01%, Paul Jones 13.46% {vsc_results}. Brian Hagen was unopposed in the Democratic primary with 998 votes {vsc_results}.
Both nominees have law enforcement backgrounds: Short is a current Knox County deputy and retired military member; Hagen is a retired Vincennes police officer and former county coroner {vsc_forum}.
No general-election forums or debates were found in the sources reviewed.

candidates.summary: Hagen served with the Vincennes Police Department from 1984 to 2022 and was Knox County coroner from 2015 to 2020; he now works for Knox County Community Corrections {vsc_forum}.
background: Vincennes Police Department, 1984–2022 (described as a former captain); courthouse security officer, 2008–2010; elected Knox County coroner, 2015–2020 {vsc_forum}.
Full-time at Knox County Community Corrections since 2024, handling transport and processing of offenders {vsc_forum}.
Cites 39 years as a law enforcement officer and military service including an overseas deployment {wtwo_five}.
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary, receiving 998 votes (unofficial) {vsc_results}.

items: Plans to work with city police, university police, schools and the Vincennes Police Department {wtwo_five}.

on_incumbent: No statements by Hagen about Sheriff Vantlin's record were found. He has said the county needs an experienced, ethical sheriff {wtwo_five}.
plans: No detailed plan for the office was found beyond his stated intent to coordinate with other local agencies and schools {wtwo_five}.
endorsements_finance: Said in a Sun-Commercial candidate profile, "I am not asking for money; all I ask for is your vote as a registered voter in Knox County, Indiana" {vsc_forum}.
No endorsements or finance reports were found.
gaps: Coverage of Hagen is thin; no campaign website or post-primary interview was found.
Search snippets indicate Hagen ran for sheriff against Vantlin in 2018 and lost a 2020 coroner race; county results pages returned 404 and these were not verified.
No statements found on the jail, staffing, budget, drugs or immigration enforcement.

candidates.summary: Short is a Knox County deputy sheriff who joined the office in 2016 after 10 years with the Stockton, California, police, and is a retired member of the military {vsc_short}. He won a four-way Republican primary {vsc_results}.
background: Joined the Knox County Sheriff's Office in 2016 after 10 years as a police officer in Stockton, California {vsc_short}.

Lists sheriff's office roles as patrol road deputy, court deputy, jail officer, field training officer, community police officer, school resource officer, rifle team member, and SWAT logistics officer and operator {vsc_short}.

Retired from the military after 21.5 years combined in the U.S. Marine Corps (infantryman, marksmanship instructor) and Army National Guard (military police), including a combat tour in Iraq {vsc_short}.
Volunteers as a lieutenant with Knox County Emergency Management and with CERT {vsc_short}.
path_to_ballot: Announced in July 2025 on his Facebook candidate page {vsc_short}.
Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary with 2,155 votes (40.55%) over Michael Fisher, John Fuller and Paul Jones (unofficial) {vsc_results}.

items: Wants to expand community policing, including "coffee with a cop" events and more high-visibility patrols in towns and rural areas {vsc_forum}.
Would coordinate with mental health providers and allied agencies {vsc_forum}.
Said he is researching ways to address stray and abused animals {vsc_forum}.
Supports releasing body camera footage and giving the public timely information, saying "This isn't new, it is being done by agencies all over the country" {vsc_forum} {wtwo_five}.

on_incumbent: No statements by Short about Sheriff Vantlin's record were found. After the primary he said he would work for everyone in the community regardless of party {wtwo_primary}.
plans: Said he would start working as soon as he is sworn in {wtwo_primary}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance figures were found in the sources reviewed.
gaps: No campaign website found; his Facebook candidate page was not reviewed.
Sun-Commercial descriptions of his years in law enforcement vary slightly ("18th year" in July 2025; "19-year" officer in March 2026).
No statements found on the jail, budget, drugs or immigration enforcement.
A search snippet said Knox County has cooperated with ICE through a 287(g) agreement; not confirmed in any page read (the August 2026 Sun-Commercial article does not mention 287(g)).
